Server Browser/Install
Install the Horizon mod

Set it up once.
Then start playing.

Horizon compiles a native .hnmod into its own client. Follow these four steps with a dedicated instance.

Download the mod

Get server-browser-2.1.0.hnmod. It contains the native Rust implementation for Horizon, rather than a Fabric or Forge .jar.

Choose the correct instance

Open that instance's game folder and put the file in horizon-native-mods. Keep an older Server Browser package backed up outside this folder.

horizon-native-mods

Enable and build the mod

On the launcher's Mods page, switch server_browser 2.1.0 on. Choose the ordinary Build action for the tested revision and review the mod list. The player decides whether to accept “I trust these mods: build”.

Launch the completed build

Wait for the build to finish, close the older client and start this exact instance. Open Multiplayer. A mod update requires a new native build; normal launches reuse it.

Native mods run with your user permissions. The first build downloads tools and can take several minutes. Your own Minecraft resources are required and are not distributed with the mod.

“No native mod is enabled”

An installed file may still be switched off. Turn on server_browser in the selected instance's Mods page.

“Installed, not built into this game”

The running client was built without this version. Finish the native build and restart the resulting instance.

An incompatible revision or E_INVALID_HELPER

Use the ordinary Build action with the package's exact pins. The separate latest-Nightly rebuild can override them. Other mods may require different revisions; test this mod alone first.
